component.name: RAMpire
component.summary: Share one pool of memory between the VMs on a KVM host

description.p: Give every virtual machine the memory it needs, when it needs it, instead of the most it might ever need. RAMpire grows a Linux VM's memory while it is busy and takes the spare back when it is idle, so the RAM you own goes where the work is.

A small service in each guest watches its memory and asks for more or gives some back. The controller on the host decides, within one shared pool, the limits you set for each VM and a reserve the host always keeps, and resizes the VM live with virtio-mem.

ul.li: One shared pool instead of every VM holding its maximum
A host reserve, and a minimum and maximum for each VM
Priorities that decide who is served first when memory is short
A full-screen view of the pool and every VM, updated live
Adding a VM in one step: its definition fixed and its guest service installed
Checks that say what is wrong and how to fix it, and rollback of any change

description.p: Open RAMpire to set the host up and add your first VM. It asks for your password, since it manages the host's VMs.

screenshot.caption: The pool, its history and every VM, live in the terminal
How RAMpire moves memory between VMs

description.p: The first release: the controller for a Linux KVM host and the Linux guest service, as packages for x86-64.
